notes.md: - Vision document unveiled by CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** on **13 December 2024** at Vijayawada (NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman **Suman Bery** present); theme **"10 Principles – One Vision"** (not "One State – One Vision"); prepared with **NITI Aayog** inputs and aligned with **Viksit Bharat @2047**.

- **10 guiding principles = Padi Sutralu** (not 5, 7, 9, 12 or 15) – PYQ (APPSC Endowment Mains asked the number: **10**):

| No. | Sutram |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Zero Poverty** (through **P4**) |
| 2 | Population Management and Human Resource Development |
| 3 | Employment and Skilling |
| 4 | Water Security (river interlinking) |
| 5 | Farmer and Agri-Tech Advancement |
| 6 | Global-Best Logistics |
| 7 | Cost Optimisation in Energy and Fuel |
| 8 | Product Perfection |
| 9 | Swachh Andhra |
| 10 | Deep-Tech in All Sectors |

- Do not confuse the 10 Sutralu with the **12 thematic sectors** of the same vision.

- Targets by **2047**: a **$2.4 trillion** economy (now about $180 billion) and per capita income about **$42,000** (about ₹55 lakh); growth of **15%** a year or more.

> Trap: USD 2.4 trillion is the economy, USD 42,000 (not 24,000 or 4,200) the per capita income; the vision drew on NITI Aayog, not the Finance Commission.

~~ Sources: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.14 ($2.4 trillion, $42,000), p.98 (15% growth), p.302 (P4), p.305-307 (Ten Sutras, 12 thematic sectors), p.310 (Wealthy, Healthy, Happy); ThePrint / Deccan Chronicle 13 Dec 2024 ("10 Principles-One Vision", release with Suman Bery) via web search; CARE APPSC Feb 2026 p.14 (P4)
- **Tirupati district** (Collector S. Venkateswar): 18% growth; 15,000+ MSMEs, 2.5 lakh jobs. India needs 7.85 million non-farm jobs a year by 2030.
- Main Budget presented by Finance Minister **Payyavula Keshav** (his **third** consecutive Budget) on **14 February 2026** – not the CM, Pawan Kalyan or Nara Lokesh.

- **Outstanding debt:** **₹6,35,177 crore = 36.04% of GSDP** (2025-26 RE); expected **₹7,11,094 crore** (about ₹7.11 lakh crore) by end of 2026-27; steady at about **36%** of GSDP (36% also in 2024-25; 33% in 2021-22).
- **Gross borrowings (public debt receipts) BE 2026-27:** **₹97,315.41 crore**; net public debt ₹75,168 crore.

> Trap: ₹97,315 crore is one year's fresh borrowing; ₹7.11 lakh crore is the outstanding debt stock; 3.8% is the fiscal deficit, not the debt ratio; 36% is debt/GSDP, not interest (about 16% of revenue receipts).

- The FRBM **Bill** was introduced in Parliament in **2000**; AP's own **AP Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2005** (AP Act 34 of 2005, 27 Oct 2005; enacted on the recommendation of the **Twelfth Finance Commission**) sets the State's deficit and debt targets – both are traps for "the FRBM Act year" (answer **2003**).

- **16th FC** (2026-31; Chair **Arvind Panagariya**; **Article 280**, constituted every five years): States' share kept at **41%**; it dropped the 15th FC's **revenue-deficit**, sector-specific and State-specific grants.

- A **separate** Agriculture and Allied Sectors Budget, presented by Agriculture Minister **K. Atchannaidu** (his **third**, after Nov 2024 and Feb 2025; not the Finance Minister) in the Assembly on **14 Feb 2026** (in the Council by **Anagani Satya Prasad**).

- Outlay: about **₹53,753 crore** (₹53,752.12 crore) – a **regrouping within** the ₹3.32 lakh crore main budget, not an addition (the agriculture and allied head of the main budget alone is **₹13,598 crore**).
- **Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan:** **₹6,600 crore** proposed for 2026-27 (₹6,660 crore was released in 2025-26 at ₹20,000 a farmer family).
- Farm mechanisation: ₹139.65 crore (app CA; The Hans India reports ₹136 crore at 50% subsidy).
- Agriculture = **33.20%** of GSDP (about one-third, not half); **62%** of the population depends on agriculture and allied activities; AP produces about 10% of India's agricultural output.

- **GSDP** 2025-26 (advance estimates, current prices): **₹17.62 lakh crore** (₹17,62,357 crore), up from ₹15.91 lakh crore = nominal growth **10.75%** (above the national average; not 10.43%, which is the per capita income growth).
- **Q2 2025-26 growth:** **11.28%** vs all-India GDP **8.7%** (current prices); The Hindu (Aug 2026) puts AP's growth over **2024-26 at 11.3%** (Telangana 10.7%).

- Target for 2026-27 (district strategies under Swarna Andhra): GSDP **₹20.36 lakh crore**, growth **15.53%** (revised from the **17.1%** target of Sept 2025); the Budget itself assumes ₹19,75,073 crore (12%).

- **Polavaram:** over **₹6,000 crore**.

- Gazette notification (**4 May 2026**); **headquarters Visakhapatnam**; operational from **1 June 2026** (earlier planned for 1 April 2026) as India's **18th railway zone** – Railways adopted a new logo with **18 stars**; GM **Sandeep Mathur**; about **3,532 route km**, works **₹54,479 crore** (app notes).

- **Four divisions:** **Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada** and **Visakhapatnam** (renamed Waltair division) – **Rajahmundry is not** a division; parts of East Coast Railway's **Rayagada division** (Palasa–Ichchapuram, Naupada–Parlakhemundi–Bobbili–Salur, etc.) merged into Visakhapatnam division.
- **South Central Railway** (est. **1966**, HQ **Secunderabad**) keeps the **Secunderabad, Hyderabad and Nanded** divisions; **East Coast Railway**: est. **2003**, HQ **Bhubaneswar**.

- **Origin:** **AP Reorganisation Act 2014, Thirteenth Schedule** (Infrastructure, item 8) – Indian Railways to **examine** a new railway zone for AP within six months; zone announced **27 Feb 2019**; **Union Cabinet approval February 2025**; **PM Narendra Modi** laid the foundation stone of the SCoR HQ (about ₹149 crore, Mudasarlova, **Visakhapatnam**) on **8 Jan 2025**.

> Exam angle: a PYQ on SCoR statements and an NH foundation-stone PYQ make this the most-asked block of the topic.

- **13,000+** tribal women and girl students (official Guinness count **13,102**) in 260 groups of 50, over about 8 acres, to an Odia folk song; **Dhimsa (Thimsa)** = tribal folk dance of **North Andhra and Odisha**; Guinness World Records est. 1955, London.

- Announced **October 2025**: **$15 billion over five years** (about ₹1.25 lakh crore; 2026-2030) – **Google's largest investment in India** and its largest AI hub outside the USA; the project moved from **Karnataka** to AP ("**competitive federalism**" row). Implementing entity **Raiden Infotech India** (Google subsidiary, with **Adani Infra**) – cleared by the **SIPB** (₹87,520 crore) and the AP Cabinet; partners **AdaniConneX** and **Airtel Nxtra**.
- **Foundation stone: 28 April 2026** by CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** at **Tarluvada** near Visakhapatnam – a **1 GW hyperscale AI data centre** (₹1.35 lakh crore over **601.4 acres**, among India's largest single FDI projects; also 160 acres at Adavivaram–Mudasarlova; 480 acres in the 2025 SIPB plan) with high-performance computing and an **international subsea cable landing**.
- Incentives (2025): **15 years free power**; water at 25% of cost for 10 years; land at concessional rates; **100% SGST reimbursement – ₹2,245 crore**; about 200 direct jobs. Aligned with **Digital Economy Vision 2030** and NITI Aayog's **National Strategy for AI**.
- Long-term **6.5 GW** digital hub (6.5 GW attracted to Visakhapatnam by Aug 2026); policy for multi-GW data centres on the **Vizag–Kapuluppada corridor**; Ashwini Vaishnaw: Visakhapatnam could become "**AI-patnam**". Five proposed data centres need about **5 TMC** of water (Godavari-Uttarandhra plan).

- Three cable landing stations → AP = **India's third subsea gateway** after **Mumbai and Chennai**; Microsoft's I-2SEA (to Q4 2029). The Vizag landing is to link **Australia, US West Coast, West Asia** and the **Cape of Good Hope** route; Vizag could become the **second major gateway on the eastern seaboard**; avoids the Red Sea cable risk of west-coast routes.

Project facts: **National Multipurpose Irrigation Project** on the **Godavari** near **Ramayyapeta** (irrigation, drinking water, hydropower, flood mitigation) – **National Project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**; on **NITI Aayog** advice the **State builds it and the Centre funds it**; **Polavaram Project Authority** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**; live storage **75.20 TMC** at FRL **+45.72 m (150 ft)** – gross **194.6 TMC** (initial height 41.11 m – 124.2 TMC); diverts **80 TMC** of Godavari water to the **Krishna** basin.
- Canals: **Left Main Canal** – East Godavari, Visakhapatnam, 4 lakh acres; **Right Main Canal** – West Godavari, Krishna, 3.2 lakh acres; new command area **7.2 lakh acres**, stabilisation 13.5 lakh acres. Headworks **80%** complete (Feb 2026); the CM ordered completion by **July 2027**, ahead of the **Godavari Pushkaralu 2027** (later target **March 2027**); **Budget 2026-27: ₹6,105 crore**; inter-State coordination with **Telangana and Chhattisgarh**.
- Wider plan: **36** irrigation projects worth **₹35,000 crore** in 3 years (2026–2028: **25 pending + 11 new**); also Pattiseema, Purushothapatnam, Veligonda.
- **Vijayawada metro** also approved – the State had approved Phase-I in Dec 2024: **Vijayawada** ₹11,009 crore, 2 corridors, 38.40 km, 34 stations (Visakhapatnam then 4 corridors, 76.90 km).

- **Medical colleges**: 10 new colleges under **PPP** from **2027-28** - Adoni, Madanapalle, Markapuram, Pulivendula, Penugonda, Palakollu, Amalapuram, Narsipatnam, Bapatla, Parvatipuram. Of **17 new government medical colleges** planned, at least **10 are on PPP** with **VGF about ₹1,468 crore**; the **G.O. of 9 September 2025** cleared the first four (**Adoni, Markapuram, Madanapalle, Pulivendula**); model **DBFOT** with Annual Concession Fee; each **150 MBBS** and **24 PG** seats; **50% government quota**; **70% beds** for **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva**, 30% market pricing; on **22 April 2026** the CM directed construction to begin **within one month**.

- Phase 1.0: 4,000 km cement roads (4,300 km in the Pallepandaga 2.0 comparison), 22,514 cattle sheds (22,500 Mini Gokulams), 21,000 farm ponds, horticulture on 64,000 acres. **Phase 2.0** (Dy CM **Pawan Kalyan**): **53,382 works**, **₹6,700 crore** – **8,000 km** rural roads, **25,000 Mini Gokulams**, also 15,750 cattle sheds, 15,500 water troughs, 82,000 soak pits.
~~ Sources: the app's current notes for this row (old-notes.txt); Praveen CA-360 Jan 2026 magazine p.53 (Pallepandaga 2.0: 53,382 works, ₹6,700 crore, 8,000 km, 25,000 Mini Gokulams)

- **Great Green Wall of AP** (Department of Environment, Forests, Science & Technology under Deputy CM **K. Pawan Kalyan**) – a **5-km-wide multi-layered** bioshield along the **974 km** coastline (the project's old figure; AP's official coastline is now 1,053.07 km); three zones – **mangroves and shelterbelts at the seaward edge / river mouths**, **windbreaks on canal bunds and roadside avenues**, **village agroforestry and community plantations**; target: restore **1 lakh ha** and protect about **33 lakh** people living within 5 km of the coast.
- Funding: MGNREGS, CAMPA, **Green Credit Program**, District Mineral Funds, climate finance. AP = **fourth most affected State by coastal erosion** – **32%** of its coastline eroding; hotspots Krishna and Godavari estuaries.

~~ Sources: Praveen CA-360 Jan 2026 magazine p.52 (Great Green Wall: 5 km, 974 km, three zones), p.53 (Pallepandaga 2.0, Amarajeevi Jaladhara); Praveen CA-360 Feb 2026 magazine p.38 (army ants, SV National Park); MISHTI: Rocket CA 2026 Part 01 p.30; mangrove directive and herbal garden: app's current notes; app notes 6:17 (sub 5) for the layers, target, funding and erosion data

- AP gets **11** sector-specific parks under Centre's **Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA)** – **100 parks** nationally, **2026-27 to 2031-32**, **₹33,660 crore**; **4,757 acres** allotted in AP; **APIIC** (est. 1973, Mangalagiri) = State nodal agency; a State-level committee monitors.

- **Aluminium Park - Srikakulam**; **Cocoa Processing Park**; **Robotics Park - Sri Sathya Sai**; **Semiconductor Park - Tirupati**. The Aug 2026 list also had **Space City (Tirupati)**, **Drone City (Kurnool)**, **Tekulodu Aerospace & Defence (Sri Sathya Sai)**, **Makavaripalem food park (Anakapalli)**, **RE zone (Prakasam)** and **Veldurthi textiles (Palnadu**, not Prakasam).

- **City Economic Region (CER)** scheme (Union Budget 2026-27; challenge mode, over five years): **Visakhapatnam** selected from AP; each city **₹5,000 crore** = ₹3,500 crore Centre + ₹1,500 crore State (loans); other cities Bengaluru, Pune, Surat, Varanasi, Bhubaneswar-Puri-Cuttack, Coimbatore-Erode-Tiruppur.

- **Jonnagiri Gold Mine** (Kurnool) renamed **Swarnagiri Gold Mine** by CM Naidu; commercial production from **24 June 2026** (commissioning had been planned for May 2026); 597.82 ha in Jonnagiri, G. Erragudi, Pagidirayi villages, **Tuggali mandal**; lease 2013 (gold, silver, copper, lead, zinc); operator **Geomysore Services India Pvt Ltd** (with **Thriveni** and **Deccan Gold Mines**; about ₹400 crore); **first major private gold mine in commercial production since Independence**.
- Context: India imports about **800 tonnes** of gold a year; **Hutti** produces about 1.5 tonnes a year; **Kolar Gold Fields** closed **2000**; MMDR Act 1957 (amended 2015, 2021).

- Zones: **SEZ, DTZ, FTWZ, EMC**; on the **Chennai–Bangalore Industrial Corridor (CBIC)**; AP–TN border, NH-16, Chennai–Vijayawada rail line; about **70 km from Chennai airport**; near **Krishnapatnam** and **Ennore** ports.
- Agreement signed (**February 2026**) by **Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN)**, DoT, AP Govt, **APBIL**, BSNL, APSFL – **State-led model**.
- Amended BharatNet approved by Union Cabinet on **4 August 2023**; BharatNet launched **2011** as **NOFN** (renamed BharatNet in 2015).

- **6 January 2026**, near **Bontlapalli (AP)**: **28.89 lane-km** and **10,655 t bituminous concrete** in **24 hours** (two records) – on **NH-544G**, the greenfield **Amaravati–Bengaluru Expressway**, starting at **Sadarlapalli**, Puttaparthi constituency, **Sri Sathya Sai district** (other reports: **28.95 km** in 24 hours, 8 a.m. 5 Jan → 8 a.m. 6 Jan, by "Raj Path Infrastructure", HQ Maharashtra).

- By **11 January**: **57,500 t** continuous laying (third); **156 lane-km** (26 km × 6 lanes) continuous (fourth).
- **Bituminous Concrete** = bitumen + crushed stone aggregates; the upper surface layer of roads.

> NH-544G record district = **Sri Sathya Sai**, not Visakhapatnam or Anantapur.

- **AP FIRST** (Andhra Pradesh - Future Innovation, Research, Science and Technology), set up under the **Companies Act**, moved from **Environment and Forests Dept** to **Science & Technology and Innovation Dept**; its research centre is at **Tirupati** – aerospace, defence, space, AI, cybersecurity, semiconductors, quantum, biotech, green energy.

| Garimella Balakrishna Prasad | Padma Shri (**posthumous**) | **Devotional music** – Annamacharya Sankeerthanams (category: Art) |
| Vempaty Kutumba Sastry | Padma Shri | **Sanskrit** – Advaita Vedanta, poetics (category: Literature and Education) |

- **[18 Aug 2026] National Sports Awards 2025** announced by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** (selection committee of Justice (Retd.) **Arun Kumar Mishra**):

- **[1 Jun 2026] Mogali Venkatram (Venkataram Reddy)** of AP won the **men's 800m gold** (**1:48.27**, 31 May 2026) at the **22nd Asian U20 Athletics Championships, Hong Kong** - **India's first gold** of the meet; he was picked on his show at the 24th National Junior Athletics Federation Competition, Tumakuru (April 2026); the win also earned him a place at the **World Athletics U20 Championships** (**Eugene, USA**, Hayward Field, **5-9 August 2026**).

- **AP Sports Policy 2024–29** – G.O.Ms.No.18, 10 December 2024; features: **one ground per village**; **Sports City in Amaravati** (no "sports capital at Kakinada"); aligned with **Swarna Andhra Sports Vision 2047**.

- **3% horizontal reservation** for meritorious sportspersons – first notified **20 April 2025** for **direct recruitment** (departments, local bodies, PSUs, police, excise, forest) and professional-course admissions; valid **five years or until a new policy**; **65 sports** in two disciplines; selection **without a written examination** (merit list of a **State Level Committee**, recruitment via **APPSC** and other boards); amended by **G.O.Ms.No.23, 14 May 2026** for government jobs; candidates scrutinised by **SAAP**.

~~ Sources: CARE APPSC Feb 2026 p.29 and Praveen CA-360 Jan 2026 magazine p.54 (SAAP chairman Ravi Naidu); G.O.Ms.No.23: app's current notes (not in the library); AP CA Monthly Apr 2025 p.41-42 (20 Apr 2025 notification, 3% horizontal, five years, 65 sports, SAAP, no written exam, State Level Committee); app notes 6:23 (sub 4) for the policy features

- **Before 2018** (united AP): bird **Indian Roller (Palapitta)**, flower **Water lily** – a 2010 PYQ's answer was then Water lily; **now Jasmine**. The residual-AP list was notified in **2018** by **G.O. No. 59**.
- **Araku Valley Arabica Coffee**: GI certified **1 March 2019**.
- Parade themes: **"Svatantrata Ka Mantra – Vande Mataram"** and **"Samriddhi Ka Mantra – Aatmanirbhar Bharat"** (**150 years of Vande Mataram**); **30** tableaux – **17** State/UT + 13 ministries.

- AP's **2025** tableau **"Etikoppaka Bommalu"** (eco-friendly wooden toys) won **third prize (jury category)** at the **76th** parade – AP's first central award for its tableau in 30 years; Tripura's **Kharchi Puja** tableau was 2nd.

- **Ugadi 2026** (19 Mar 2026): awards given by the CM on **20 Mar 2026** - **38 Kala Ratna (Hamsa)** + **122 Ugadi awards** (123 Ugadi Puraskaralu in some reports); Kala Ratna carries **₹50,000**, a swan statue and a certificate (Kuchipudi exponent **Dr. P. Rama Devi** – Kala Ratna 2026).

- **[22 Oct / 4 Nov 2026] National SARAS Mela-2026, Vijayawada** (**Punnami Ghat**, **13-31 October 2026**): jointly by the **Union Ministry of Rural Development**, **AP Government** and **SERP** (AP's rural poverty alleviation society); **first time held outside Delhi-NCR** (the **first National SARAS Mela was in 1999, Delhi**); over **1,500 SHG women entrepreneurs** from **30 States/UTs**; under **DAY-NRLM** (NRLM launched **2011**, renamed **2015**). **Sales:** total business **₹12.84 crore**; **AP 1st** with **₹2.99 crore (~23%)**, **UP 2nd (₹1.22 crore)**.
> ⚠ Trap: AEI 2026 topper is **Goa**, not AP (AP 2nd); in EVOI AP is **1st**; SARAS Mela 2026 at Vijayawada = first time **outside Delhi-NCR**.
> The TAAI award ceremony was in **Kolkata**, not AP.

- APSLSA Executive Chairman: by convention the **senior-most HC judge after the CJ**, appointed by the **Governor** on the **Chief Justice's recommendation** (**Legal Services Authorities Act 1987**, in force **1995**; **NALSA 1995**; **Article 39A** – equal justice and free legal aid).
- In March 2026, as a puisne judge, she was made **Executive Chairperson, AP State Legal Services Authority**; after she became CJ, **Justice Ravinath Tilhari** took the post (June 2026).

- **58-foot bronze statue of Potti Sriramulu** at **Smritivan** (6.8 acres) near **Tulluru**, inaugurated by CM Naidu – 58 feet for his **58-day fast**; tentatively approved in 2025 for his **125th birth anniversary**; 26 tons bronze, 42 tons iron; about ₹150 crore; **first massive statue in Amaravati**. Potti Sriramulu (1901–1952), "**Amarajeevi**" (immortal soul); his fast led to **Andhra State on 1 October 1953**.

- **GTM Tourism Awards 2026**: AP named **"Best Tourism Promotion State"** at **Global Travel Market (GTM) 2026** – received by Tourism Minister **Kandula Durgesh** on 4 June 2026, Thiruvananthapuram (Kovalam); AP to host **GTM Expo 2027**.
